The '''2023–24 season''' was the [[List of Manchester City F.C. seasons|129th season]] in the existence of [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City Football Club]] and their 22nd consecutive season in the [[English football league system|top flight]] of [[Football in England|English football]], where they were competing as three-time [[2022–23 Premier League|defending champions]]. As reigning [[Treble (association football)#Continental trebles|continental treble]] winners, Manchester City participated in seven competitions this season, namely the [[2023–24 Premier League|Premier League]], [[2023–24 FA Cup|FA Cup]], [[2023–24 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]], [[2023 FA Community Shield|FA Community Shield]], [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]]; entering the latter for the 13th consecutive season and as [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League|defending champions]] for the first time; [[2023 UEFA Super Cup|UEFA Super Cup]] and [[2023 FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA Club World Cup]]; also making their debut in the latter two tournaments.

City kicked off their unprecedented season on 6 August 2023 by losing the Community Shield for the third consecutive year, this time to [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]. They drew 1–1 in normal time, having conceded an equaliser in the 11th minute of injury time and lost the subsequent [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] 4–1. As such, the Blues missed out on becoming only the third European men's club to win the [[Sextuple (association football)|sextuple]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |title=Arsenal beat Man City in Community Shield shootout |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66352143 |access-date=6 August 2023}}</ref> City clinched their first trophy of the season ten days later, on 16 August, in another one-off match, overcoming [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] on penalties after a 1–1 draw [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|after extra time]] for the club's first-ever UEFA Super Cup.<ref name=":8">{{cite web |date=16 August 2023 |title=Man City beat Sevilla to Lift the First European Trophy of the 2023-24 season |url=https://offsidetrap.in/man-city-beat-sevilla-to-lift-uefa-super-cup-23-24/ |access-date=16 August 2023}}</ref> On 27 September, the Blues were knocked out of the League Cup in the third round by [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] following a 1–0 away loss.<ref name=":9">{{cite news|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/13866/12969824/newcastle-1-0-man-city-alexander-isak-strikes-during-excellent-second-half-display-from-magpies-in-carabao-cup-third-round|title=Newcastle 1-0 Man City: Alexander Isak strikes during excellent second-half display from Magpies in Carabao Cup third round|author=Peter Smith|publisher=Sky Sports|date=28 September 2023|access-date=6 October 2023}}</ref> On 22 December, City defeated [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]] 4–0 in the [[2023 FIFA Club World Cup final|Club World Cup final]] to win the competition for the first time, becoming the first English club to hold five major domestic and international titles simultaneously.<ref name=":10">{{cite news |title=Man City make history with Club World Cup win |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67795653 |date=22 December 2023 |access-date=24 December 2023}}</ref>

Manchester City's title defence in the Champions League came to an end at the quarter-final stage on 17 April 2024, when they were knocked out by [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in a penalty shoot-out after a 4–4 aggregate draw over the two legs, having met the Spanish giants in the knockout stages for the third year in a row.<ref name=":15">{{cite news |title=Man City knocked out of Champions League by Real Madrid |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/68830107 |date=17 April 2024 |access-date=21 April 2024 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref> The Blues successfully defended their Premier League title for an unprecedented fourth straight season to become the first English men's club in history to win four consecutive top-tier titles. They fought another close title race against Arsenal, sealing the result on the final day of the season with a 3–1 victory against [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] at home.<ref name=":16">{{cite news |title=Manchester City win record fourth English title in a row as Foden scores twice in 3-1 win over West Ham |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/czkvkp3ej9xt |date=19 May 2024 |access-date=19 May 2024 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref> In the FA Cup, City once again reached the [[2024 FA Cup final|final]] where they lost 1–2 to [[Manchester derby|local rivals]] [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] on 25 May, in a rematch of the [[2023 FA Cup final|previous year's final]].<ref name=":17">{{cite news |title=Manchester United win FA Cup after Garnacho and Mainoo stun City |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/article/2024/may/25/manchester-city-manchester-united-fa-cup-final-match-report |date=25 May 2024 |access-date=25 May 2024 |work=The Guardian}}</ref>

The season was the first since [[2015–16 Manchester City F.C. season|2015–16]] without German midfielder and former club captain [[İlkay Gündoğan]], who departed to [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] at the end of his contract in the summer, although he would return to City a year later, and the first since [[2016–17 Manchester City F.C. season|2016–17]] and [[2017–18 Manchester City F.C. season|2017–18]] without center back [[Aymeric Laporte]] and forward [[Riyad Mahrez]], who both departed to [[Saudi Pro League]] clubs [[Al-Ahli Saudi FC|Al Ahli]] and [[Al Nassr FC|Al Nassr]], respectively. [[Kyle Walker]] eventually replaced Gündoğan as the new club captain.

==Season summary==
===Pre-season===
In the aftermath of their historic [[Treble (association football)#Continental trebles|continental treble]]-winning season in [[2022–23 Manchester City F.C. season|2022–23]], City's main squad issues ahead of the new season were whether incumbent club captain [[İlkay Gündoğan]] would sign a new contract or leave the club on a free transfer after seven successful years;<ref>{{cite web |title=Man City Star's Future in Balance As Barcelona Turn Up The Heat |url=https://eplindex.com/90067/man-city-stars-future-in-balance-as-barcelona-turn-up-the-heat.html |access-date=17 June 2023 |website=Eplindex|date=17 June 2023 }}</ref> if [[Kyle Walker]] would be transferred ahead of his final contract year;<ref>{{cite web |last=Bray |first=Joe |date=17 June 2023 |title=Walker transfer could change Guardiola's plan for Lewis at Man City |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/walker-bayern-man-city-transfer-27143009 |access-date=17 June 2023 |publisher=Manchester Evening News}}</ref> whether [[Aymeric Laporte]] would be leaving for more playing time, following a season in which he had fallen down the pecking order for central defenders;<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brennan |first=Feargal |date=16 June 2023 |title=Barcelona target Aymeric Laporte hints at Manchester City exit |url=https://www.football-espana.net/2023/06/16/barcelona-target-aymeric-laporte-manchester-city |access-date=17 June 2023 |website=Football España}}</ref> and, after several years of pre-season speculation, if [[Bernardo Silva]] could attract an acceptable fee to allow him to move away from Manchester too.<ref>{{Cite web |author1=Mark White |date=19 June 2023 |title=Manchester City star Bernardo Silva in talks over Saudi Arabia offer: report |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/manchester-city-star-bernardo-silva-in-talks-over-saudi-arabia-offer-report |access-date=19 June 2023 |website=FourFourTwo}}</ref>

It was rumoured that City were in transfer talks with [[Mateo Kovačić]] from [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] and with [[Joško Gvardiol]] from [[RB Leipzig]] as potential replacements for Gündoğan and Laporte, respectively.<ref>{{cite web |last=Pettigrove |first=Jason |date=17 June 2023 |title=Fabrizio Romano on the difficulties Man City face in pursuit of Gvardiol and other potential moves ahead this summer |url=https://www.caughtoffside.com/2023/06/17/fabrizio-romano-on-the-difficulties-man-city-face-in-pursuit-of-gvardiol-and-other-potential-moves-ahead-this-summer/ |access-date=17 June 2023 |website=CaughtOffside}}</ref>

On 21 June, it was announced that Gündoğan would be joining [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] on the expiration of his contract after all. His last action as a City player was therefore lifting the club's first Champions League trophy as team captain.<ref name="Gundo"/> On the same day, it was reported that Manchester City had agreed a fee with Chelsea for the transfer of Kovačić.<ref>{{cite news |title=Man City agree £30m deal for Chelsea's Kovacic |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65966385 |access-date=23 June 2023}}</ref>

To further strengthen the team's midfield, City also entered a bidding race with [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] for [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham]]'s [[Declan Rice]], a player similar in profile to [[Rodri (footballer, born 1996)|Rodri]]. The club's first offer of £80 million guaranteed plus £10 million in add-ons was rejected by West Ham.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4625184/2023/06/26/manchester-city-declan-rice-offer/|title=Manchester City make formal offer for Declan Rice|author=David Ornstein|website=The Athletic|date=27 June 2023|access-date=27 June 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=West Ham reject Manchester City's offer for Declan Rice|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4643353/2023/06/27/declan-rice-transfer-man-city/|author=David Ornstein|website=The Athletic|date=27 June 2023|access-date=27 June 2023}}</ref> Man City pulled out of the race to sign Rice, after West Ham rejected Arsenal's bid of £100 million plus £5 million in add-ons, instead opting to find other players to strengthen their midfield, first being linked with [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]]'s [[Gabri Veiga]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Man City out of Declan Rice transfer race as Arsenal negotiate with West Ham |work=The Athletic |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4646753/2023/06/28/man-city-arsenal-declan-rice-transfer/ |access-date=28 June 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Manchester City have entered the race for Spanish talent Gabri Veiga after pulling out of Declan Rice deal. |work=Fabrizio Romano |url=https://twitter.com/FabrizioRomano/status/1674020710052667395?ref_src=twsrc%5Egoogle%7Ctwcamp%5Eserp%7Ctwgr%5Etweet |access-date=28 June 2023}}</ref>

Kovačić's transfer was duly announced on 27 June, for a reported initial fee of £25m plus £5m in potential add-ons.<ref>{{cite news|title=City Complete Kovacic Signing|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/mateo-kovacic-joins-manchester-city-63823479|author=Rob Pollard|publisher=Manchester City F.C.|date=27 June 2023|access-date=27 June 2023}}</ref>

On 28 July, City announced [[Riyad Mahrez]] was leaving the club after five successful years to join [[Al-Ahli Saudi FC|Al-Ahli]] in the [[Saudi Professional League]] for a £30 million fee. He was one of many high-profile players in their thirties attracted by lucrative contract offers to join the Saudi league that summer.<ref name="Mahrez" />

The transfer of Gvardiol was confirmed on 5 August after several weeks of negotiations with Leipzig for a reported fee of €90 million (£77.5 million).<ref>{{cite news |title=Man City transfer news: Pep Guardiola's side finalise £77.6m deal for RB Leipzig centre-back Josko Gvardiol |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11679/12932475/man-city-transfer-news-pep-guardiolas-side-finalise-77-6m-deal-for-rb-leipzig-centre-back-josko-gvardiol |access-date=6 August 2023 |publisher=Sky Sports}}</ref> The club confirmed he would take the 24 shirt number for the season, last worn by [[John Stones]] during his first year at City.<ref name=":0" />

The Blues started their pre-season preparations some one to two weeks later than their main rivals to account for their late finish to the previous treble-winning campaign. City played three friendly warm-up games in a tour of Japan and South Korea, where they defeated [[Yokohama F. Marinos]], a fellow [[City Football Group|CFG]] club, and [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]], but lost to [[Atlético Madrid]].

===Start of season===
City suffered a defeat for the third consecutive season in their opening competitive fixture, losing the [[2023 FA Community Shield|Community Shield]] on penalties to Arsenal after a 1–1 draw in normal time at [[Wembley Stadium]] on 6 August. [[Cole Palmer]] had scored from a wonderful curling shot in the 77th minute, but [[Leandro Trossard]] equalised in the eleventh minute of injury time when a cruel double deflection from [[Julián Alvarez]] and [[Manuel Akanji]] wrong-footed [[Stefan Ortega]]. In the subsequent penalty shoot-out, Arsenal scored all four penalties, but [[Kevin De Bruyne]]'s powerful drive hit the cross-bar and Rodri's attempt was saved by [[Aaron Ramsdale]]. Losing the English equivalent of a national [[Super cup#National super cups|super cup]] deprived Manchester City of the opportunity to become only the third European men's club to win the [[Sextuple (association football)|sextuple]].<ref name=":1"/>

Manchester City started their [[2023–24 Premier League|Premier League]] campaign with a 3–0 win over [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] at [[Turf Moor]]. [[Erling Haaland]] scored twice, and Rodri also chipped in with a goal to seal the victory.<ref>{{cite news |date=11 August 2023 |title=Manchester City beat Burnley on opening day: De Bruyne Injured, Haaland scored twice |url=https://offsidetrap.in/manchester-city-beat-burnley-de-bruyne-halland/ |website=Offside Trap |access-date=16 August 2023}}</ref> Kevin De Bruyne was substituted in the first half, and [[Pep Guardiola]] later confirmed that he had sustained a hamstring injury which could keep him out for up to four months if surgery was needed.<ref>{{cite web |date=12 August 2023 |title=Guardiola gives update on De Bruyne's Injury and Clarifies Clash with Haaland |url=https://offsidetrap.in/guardiola-gives-update-de-bruynes-injury-haaland-clash/ |website=Offside Trap |access-date=16 August 2023}}</ref>

On 16 August, City played [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] in the [[2023 UEFA Super Cup]], winning on penalties after a 1–1 draw in normal time and lifting the trophy for the first time in club history.<ref name=":8"/>

On 22 August, it was revealed that [[Pep Guardiola]] had undergone emergency back surgery and would be unavailable until recovery.<ref>{{cite news |date=22 August 2023 |title=Guardiola undergoes minor back surgery |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/pep-guardiola-back-surgery-63828302 |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |access-date=22 August 2023}}</ref> During this time, assistant manager [[Juanma Lillo]] took charge, winning two games against [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] away and [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] at home by the scores of 2–1 and 5–1 respectively. The latter game included Haaland's first hat-trick of the season as he became the fastest player to score 40 Premier League goals (in just 39 games), beating the previous records set by Andrew Cole and Alan Shearer.<ref name=":7" />

In the final days of the transfer window City brought in exciting Belgian winger [[Jérémy Doku]] from [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]], to effectively replace Mahrez, and creative Portuguese midfielder [[Matheus Nunes]] from [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]], both for fees in excess of £50 million.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /> In the other direction, [[Aymeric Laporte]] left the club as expected to join [[Al Nassr FC|Al Nassr]] in the Saudi League, [[João Cancelo]] joined Barcelona for a season-long loan, and academy graduate [[Cole Palmer]] joined Chelsea for a fee in excess of £40 million.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6" />

By the time of the first [[FIFA International Match Calendar|international break]] of the season on 3 September, City were the only remaining Premier League club with a 100% win record and topped the standings by a two-point margin. On 16 September, the Blues extended their winning start in the league to five games by defeating West Ham 3–1 at the [[London Stadium]], with goals from new signing Jeremy Doku, Bernardo Silva and Erling Haaland.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/12309/12961105/west-ham-1-3-manchester-city-pep-guardiola-returns-to-oversee-impressive-win-as-erling-haaland-scores-seventh-of-season|title=West Ham 1-3 Manchester City: Pep Guardiola returns to oversee impressive win as Erling Haaland scores seventh of season|author=Laura Hunter|publisher=Sky Sports|date=16 September 2023|access-date=23 September 2023}}</ref>

City's winning run came to an abrupt end at [[St James' Park]] vs [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] in the [[2023–24 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] third round, with the Blues being shut out by a reinvigorated [[Eddie Howe]] side and exiting the competition at the first hurdle.<ref name=":9"/> This was followed by the first league defeat after six consecutive victories at [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolves]], with Alvarez scoring an equalising free kick in an eventual 1–2 loss.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/12971659/wolves-2-1-man-city-champions-perfect-start-to-premier-league-season-ended-in-surprise-molineux-defeat|title=Wolves 2-1 Man City: Champions' perfect start to Premier League season ended in surprise Molineux defeat|author=Joe Shread|publisher=Sky Sports|date=30 September 2023|access-date=6 October 2023}}</ref>

===Autumn period===
Manchester City began October with a second consecutive league defeat, this time at Arsenal, losing 0–1 due to a late [[Gabriel Martinelli]] winner.<ref>{{cite web |title=Arsenal v Man City, 2023/24 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/93391 |access-date=4 November 2023 |publisher=Premier League}}</ref> This meant the Blues had lost all three games where Rodri served a suspension for a red card he received against [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] in September, and they dropped below unbeaten Arsenal and [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham]] in the league table. However, City's good form soon returned and they notably beat their [[Manchester derby|closest rivals]] [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] 3–0 at [[Old Trafford]] in the season's first [[List of association football rivalries in the United Kingdom#North-West England and Yorkshire|derby match]] and achieved the biggest winning margin so far by defeating [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]] 6–1 at home. The latter game included four assists and a goal from Doku, who set a new club record, equalled the Premier League record for most assists in a single match and, at the age of 21 years and 161 days, became both the youngest player in Premier League history with five goal involvements and the youngest player to assist four goals in a single game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Man Utd v Man City, 2023/24 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/93418 |access-date=4 November 2023 |publisher=Premier League}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Man City v Bournemouth, 2023/24 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/93426 |access-date=4 November 2023 |publisher=Premier League}}</ref>

A comfortable 3–0 home victory against [[BSC Young Boys|Young Boys]] on 7 November ensured that title holders City would participate in the [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|knockout stages of the Champions League]] for the 11th consecutive season with two group games to spare.<ref>{{cite web |title=Man City-Young Boys: UEFA Champions League 2023/24 Group stage |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2039135--man-city-vs-young-boys/ |access-date=7 November 2023 |website=UEFA}}</ref>

Two league draws either side of the final autumn international break: an exciting game against Chelsea at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]] that ended 4–4 and a 1–1 draw against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] at home; left City in second place, a point behind Arsenal with a third of the season played. The Blues ended November coming back from two goals down to beat [[RB Leipzig]] 3–2 and win their Champions League group for the seventh consecutive season with a game to spare and preserve their record unbeaten streak and winning home streak in the competition.<ref>{{cite web |title=Man City-Leipzig: UEFA Champions League 2023/24 Group stage |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2039151--man-city-vs-leipzig/ |access-date=30 November 2023 |website=UEFA}}</ref>

A third consecutive league draw against Tottenham at the start of December at home was followed by City's third league defeat of the season by a single goal away to an in-form [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] who moved above them in the table. The champions had now not won a league game for a month and were in fourth place in the league table, six points behind leaders Arsenal.<ref>{{cite web |title=Aston Villa v Man City, 2023/24 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/93461 |access-date=8 December 2023 |publisher=Premier League}}</ref>

This barren run was finally ended at [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton]] on 10 December, with a 2–1 victory, despite the absence of goalscoring talisman Haaland due to injury.<ref>{{cite web |title=Luton v Man City, 2023/24 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/93476 |access-date=14 December 2023 |publisher=Premier League}}</ref> The final Champions League group game against [[Red Star Belgrade]] on 13 December was a [[dead rubber]] with both sides' final positions already confirmed. Guardiola used this as an opportunity to make nine changes to the team and give debuts to a few [[Manchester City F.C. EDS and Academy|academy]] players and playing time to less often selected first team players. All three City goalscorers in the subsequent 3–2 victory, [[Micah Hamilton]], [[Oscar Bobb]] and [[Kalvin Phillips]], scored their first senior City goals, with Hamilton scoring on his first team debut, and the victory meant City had completed a Champions League group with maximum points for the first time in their history.<ref>{{cite web |title=Crvena zvezda-Man City: UEFA Champions League 2023/24 Group stage |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2039171--crvena-zvezda-vs-man-city/ |access-date=14 December 2023 |website=UEFA}}</ref>

On 16 December, [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] were able to pull back from being two goals down to inflict City's third consecutive home league draw and fourth league draw in six games, leaving them fourth in the table and five points behind leaders Arsenal.<ref>{{cite news |title=Palace deny Man City win with 95th-minute penalty |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67667797 |access-date=24 December 2023}}</ref> The Blues would drop to fifth and the gap to the top widened to six points by [[Christmas]], as City's final pre-holiday game against [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] had been postponed due to their participation in the [[2023 FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA Club World Cup]].

Manchester City travelled to [[Jeddah]] in [[Saudi Arabia]] as favourites and duly returned as world champions, having beaten [[2022 AFC Champions League|AFC Champions League]] champions [[Urawa Red Diamonds]] 3–0 in the semi-finals and [[2023 Copa Libertadores|Copa Libertadores]] champions [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]] 4–0 in the [[2023 FIFA Club World Cup final|final]] to lift the trophy at their first attempt.<ref name=":10" /> They became the first English team to hold five major domestic and continental titles simultaneously, and Guardiola emerged as the first coach to win the Club World Cup with three separate clubs, having previously succeeded at Barcelona and Bayern Munich. City would be the last team to win the title in its current format as the competition was to be expanded from seven to 32 participating clubs for the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup|2025 edition]].

===Christmas and New Year===
City came back from a goal down for the second consecutive away game to defeat [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] 3–1 on their return to domestic football on 27 December,<ref>{{cite news |title=Champions Man City come from behind to beat Everton |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67768993 |access-date=27 December 2023}}</ref> and remained undefeated over the holiday season to end 2023 third in the league standings, five points behind leaders Liverpool with a game in hand.

The Blues kicked off their [[2023–24 FA Cup|FA Cup]] campaign with a convincing 5–0 home victory over [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]] in the third round, with two goals from [[Phil Foden]] and an assist from Kevin De Bruyne who was returning for his first appearance since suffering a [[hamstring]] injury in August. The team's final game before the mid-winter break on 13 January saw them win 3–2 at St James' Park in an exciting encounter against Newcastle United. City came back from 1–2 down with an injury time winner from youngster [[Oscar Bobb]] and a goal and an assist from De Bruyne in a 20-minute [[Cameo appearance|cameo]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Bobb scores late winner for Man City at Newcastle |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67900157 |access-date=13 January 2024 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

[[Kalvin Phillips]] was loaned to West Ham for the remainder of the season after City returned from a week of warm weather training in [[Abu Dhabi]].<ref name="Phillips" /> On 26 January, [[Nathan Aké]] scored an 88th-minute winner to beat Spurs 1–0 away in the fourth round of the FA Cup and qualify for the last 16. This was the club's first goal at the [[Tottenham Hotspur Stadium]], scored in City's sixth fixture there since it opened in 2019 and after 102 goal attempts.<ref>{{cite news |title=Late Ake winner ensures Man City knock out Spurs |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/68097502 |access-date=27 January 2024 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

Phil Foden scored his second senior career [[Hat-trick#Association football|hat-trick]] as the Blues won 3–1 at Brentford's [[Brentford Community Stadium|Gtech Community Stadium]] on 5 February. The victory put Manchester City within two points of leaders Liverpool with a game in hand.<ref name=":12" />

A brace from Erling Haaland, marking the first time he scored since his return from a two-month injury lay-off, were enough to defeat Everton 2–0 at home in an early kick-off on 10 February. The win put City ahead in the league standings for the first time since October, albeit briefly until Liverpool won against Burnley later that day.

On resumption of the Champions League, City beat [[F.C. Copenhagen|Copenhagen]] 3–1 away from home on 13 February in the first leg of the round of 16. De Bruyne scored and assisted, having contributed eight goal involvements since his return from injury four weeks before.

By the end of February, Manchester City had extended their unbeaten run to 18 games in all competitions, taking them to within a point of leaders Liverpool and a point ahead of third-placed Arsenal in what was turning out to be a three-way title race. The Blues ended the month with a convincing 6–2 victory at [[Kenilworth Road]] against Luton Town in the FA Cup fifth round. Erling Haaland scored five goals in a single match for the second time in his short City career, with Kevin De Bruyne assisting four of them.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Haaland scores five as Man City thrash Luton |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68417647 |access-date=2024-02-28 |work=BBC Sport |language=en}}</ref>

===Season run-in===
City were due to face a home derby and all of the other top-four sides in a crucial run of games in March and early April, which could go a long way to decide the destination of the league title. They started with a 3–1 victory against the local rivals, coming back from a goal down after a 25-yard [[Marcus Rashford]] strike with a dominant display and a brace of well-taken Phil Foden goals.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Foden double helps Man City fight back to win derby |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68395537 |access-date=2024-03-03 |work=BBC Sport |language=en}}</ref> This was the first time in the Premier League era that City had come from behind to beat United and the first time in 143 competitive games that United had lost when leading at half-time. It was also Rodri's 59th consecutive appearance for City without experiencing defeat, a new Premier League record.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-03-03 |title=Man City's Rodri breaks record that has stood for 16 years after Man Utd victory |url=https://www.sportbible.com/football/football-news/man-city/man-city-rodri-man-utd-premier-league-174209-20240303 |access-date=2024-03-03 |website=SPORTbible |language=en}}</ref>

On 6 March, the Champions League holders swept aside Copenhagen 6–2 on aggregate to reach the quarter-finals for the seventh successive season and become the first English club to win 10 consecutive matches in the competition, and the first side in major European competition history to score 3+ goals in nine consecutive home games, a run which started with a 5–0 win over Copenhagen back in October 2022.<ref>{{cite news|title =Man City 3-1 Copenhagen (6-2 agg): 'We are a team that believes we can do it' - Pep Guardiola|work=BBC Sport |date=7 March 2024 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/68497653|access-date=7 March 2024}}</ref>

City drew 1–1 against Liverpool at [[Anfield]] on 10 March. The Blues had been ahead from a well-executed set piece corner that led to John Stones' first goal of the season, but Liverpool equalised via a penalty awarded after [[Ederson (footballer, born 1993)|Ederson]] had fouled [[Darwin Núñez|Núñez]] while dealing with an under hit Aké back-pass. This meant City slipped to third place, a point behind both new leaders Arsenal and Liverpool.

Two deflected goals from Bernardo Silva in the first half were enough in a comfortable 2–0 victory over Newcastle in the FA Cup quarter-finals on 16 March, taking Manchester City to the semi-finals at Wembley for a record-breaking sixth season in a row and seventh time in Guardiola's eight seasons at the club.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Man City dispatch Newcastle to reach FA Cup semis |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68573294 |access-date=16 March 2024 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

Arsenal held City to a 0–0 draw at the [[City of Manchester Stadium]] on 31 March, leaving the Blues in third place. However, victories against Aston Villa at home and Crystal Palace away kept pressure on the leading two clubs. These games were also notable for including Phil Foden's second hat-trick of the season, taking him to over 20 goals for the first time in his professional career; and a brace from Kevin De Bruyne which marked his 100th goal scored for the club.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Man City and Arsenal draw to hand Liverpool advantage |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68648918 |access-date=6 April 2024 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Foden scores hat-trick as Man City beat Villa |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68672065 |access-date=6 April 2024 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=De Bruyne shines as Man City maintain title challenge |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68697135 |access-date=6 April 2024 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref> With Liverpool drawing at Manchester United on 7 April, City were now a point behind both Arsenal and Liverpool with seven games to go.<ref>{{Cite news |title=How Manchester United held Liverpool to draw on goals by Kobbie Mainoo, Bruno Fernandes |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/live-blogs/manchester-united-liverpool-live-updates-premier-league-score-result/svlGoNslyXIA/ |access-date=8 April 2024 |work=The Athletic |date=7 April 2024 }}</ref>

In the first leg of their Champions League quarter-finals against [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] on 9 April at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]], City were missing both their first choice full-backs Walker and Aké due to injuries picked up in the last international break and De Bruyne spent the entire match on the bench with a bout of [[gastroenteritis]]. Madrid players had also recently benefited from a nine-day rest, while City played two league matches at the start of April. In the game, Bernardo Silva opened the scoring with a low shot from a free kick after just two minutes, before [[Eduardo Camavinga]] and [[Rodrygo]] gave Real the lead with two deflected goals a minute apart. In the second half, City applied more pressure and levelled in the 66th minute through a Phil Foden strike from the edge of the area into the top corner and then went ahead five minutes later when Joško Gvardiol produced another stunning long range shot to score his first goal for the club. [[Federico Valverde]]'s superb volley in the 79th rescued a draw for Real, and the match ended 3–3.

Manchester City moved back to lead the league table by two points after an eventful weekend on the following matchday. The Blues comfortably beat Luton 5–1 at home on 13 April as Guardiola rested several key players in anticipation of the upcoming second leg against Madrid. Both City's title rivals were then beaten the following day at home: Liverpool by Crystal Palace and Arsenal by Aston Villa.<ref>{{Cite news |title='Six finals to go' - who will win the Premier League? |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68481769 |access-date=16 April 2024 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 17 April, City were dramatically eliminated by Real Madrid in the reverse leg at the City of Manchester Stadium. An early goal from [[Rodrygo]] was cancelled out in the 76th minute by a Kevin De Bruyne strike in a game dominated by City possession and resolute defending from Madrid. With no further goals the match ended 4–4 after extra time on aggregate and duly went to penalties. Despite [[Luka Modrić]] missing Madrid's first attempt, ''Los Blancos'' ran out 4–3 winners, with Bernardo Silva's attempted [[Panenka (penalty kick)|panenka]] being easily saved and another from substitute Kovačić also saved by keeper [[Andriy Lunin]].<ref name=":15"/>

Three days later, the Blues were at Wembley Stadium to play their FA Cup semi-final against Chelsea. Chelsea forward [[Nicolas Jackson]] had several promising chances to score during the match but failed to convert them. An 84th-minute goal from Bernardo Silva eventually proved to be the difference. City would play their closest rivals Manchester United in the [[2024 FA Cup final|final]] for the second consecutive season, who had scraped past [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]] in the other semi-final on penalties.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Late Silva goal sends Man City into FA Cup final |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68860454 |access-date=21 April 2024 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Man Utd scrape past Coventry to reach FA Cup final |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68860463 |access-date=21 April 2024 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

===End of season===
Two away wins the following week; 4–0 at [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton]] and 2–0 at Nottingham Forest, respectively; ensured City remained in second place, a point behind Arsenal with a game in hand and just three games remaining for the league leaders. Liverpool's title challenge had by then been curtailed in dropping points to Everton and West Ham, leaving them in third, four points behind the Blues with a game less to play. City won all five league games in April and were by then on a club record 31 game unbeaten streak in all competitions.<ref>{{cite news |date=28 April 2024 |title=Haaland scores as Man City fend off Forest |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/68867478 |access-date=28 April 2024 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

Both Arsenal and City continued their winning streaks up to their penultimate games, including an Arsenal victory by 1–0 at [[Old Trafford]], and a first City league goal and league win at the Tottenham Hotspurs Stadium in a tense 2–0 win, which included a 89th minute save by deputy goalkeeper [[Stefan Ortega]] from a [[Son Heung-min]] one on one chance which would have set the score at 1–1. Ortega had come on for an injured [[Ederson (footballer, born 1993)|Ederson]] in the second half. Haaland scored both goals with a tap in from a Kevin De Bruyne assist and an injury time penalty after [[Jérémy Doku|Doku]] had been fouled by [[Pedro Porro]].<ref>{{cite web |date=14 May 2024 |title=Tottenham vs Man City LIVE: Result, team news, commentary & updates |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cv2x7lzdd1zt |access-date=18 May 2024 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=12 May 2024 |title=Man Utd vs Arsenal LIVE: Premier League score, radio commentary & text updates |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cn0rndpvx20t |access-date=18 May 2024 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> Both games were played in front of uncertain fans of their rivals closest rivals, supposedly torn between supporting their team and hoping their rivals would be denied a title win, although United fans were far less likely to support Arsenal, owing to their own [[Arsenal F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|fierce rivalry]] with the Gunners.

These results meant City would go into the final round of fixtures two points ahead of Arsenal on points, but a goal behind on goal difference, meaning a victory against West Ham at home would be enough to secure their fourth consecutive league title but dropping points could let Arsenal back in with a victory against Everton at the [[Emirates Stadium]].<ref>{{cite web |date=18 May 2024 |title=Premier League final-day: Title race, European qualification and Klopp's farewell |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/crgyg9d70n7o |access-date=18 May 2024 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 3 May, Phil Foden was named [[FWA Footballer of the Year]], the season's first top level award.<ref name=":13" /> On the eve of the season's penultimate matches, it was announced that Foden had been voted the [[Premier League Player of the Season]] to add to his FWA award. It was the fifth consecutive season that a City player had won this award.<ref name=":14" />

A Foden goal after 74 seconds in the final league game set City on their way to what turned out to be a comfortable 3–1 victory against West Ham that sealed their historic fourth consecutive title win at the City of Manchester Stadium. Foden ended up scoring a first half brace and, although West Ham got a goal back through a stunning [[Mohammed Kudus]] [[bicycle kick]], Rodri sealed the victory with a third goal in the 59th minute and the blues held on until the final whistle to deny Arsenal despite their late 2–1 victory at home to Everton.<ref name=":16" /> Haaland had won the [[Premier League Golden Boot]] award for both his inaugural seasons with his 27 league goals.<ref name=":19">{{cite news |last=Mumford |first=Jack |date=19 May 2024 |title=Haaland wins second successive Premier League Golden Boot |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/erling-haaland-premier-league-golden-boot-may-2024-man-city-63851731 |access-date=19 May 2024 |publisher=Manchester City F.C.}}</ref> Guardiola had won the [[Premier League Manager of the Season]] for the second consecutive season and the fifth time overall.<ref name=":20" />

City could now go onto to become the first English club to complete consecutive [[Double (association football)#England|league and FA Cup doubles]]. However, first-half goals from [[Alejandro Garnacho]] and [[Kobbie Mainoo]] were sufficient for Manchester United to deny the favourites and win 2–1 at Wembley. City had the majority of the possession throughout the game, but Guardiola was forced to make changes at half time after an innocuous first half, bringing on [[Jérémy Doku]] and sacrificing the midfield double pivot provided by [[Mateo Kovačić]]. Doku duly got a goal back in the 87th minute but City were to be denied an equaliser through a combination of good defending, the woodwork and wayward finishing.<ref name=":17" /> The defeat ended City's club record 35-game unbeaten run (the second-longest in league history) and Rodri's remarkable 74-game unbeaten streak in all competitions.<ref>{{cite web |date=25 May 2024 |title=FA Cup Final 2024 LIVE: Watch Man City vs Man Utd stream plus score, line-ups, commentary & latest updates from Wembley |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c2jj8k5vym5t |access-date=29 May 2024 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

The following day after the FA Cup final defeat, Foden was announced as the club's Etihad Player of the Season after an online poll of fans.<ref name=":18">{{cite news |last=Jack |first=Mumford |date=26 May 2024 |title=Foden wins 2023/24 Etihad Player of the Season |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/phil-foden-etihad-player-of-the-season-winner-63852324 |access-date=26 May 2024 |publisher=Manchester City F.C.}}</ref> Foden was also awarded the [[PFA Players' Player of the Year]] award shortly after the start of the following season to give him the hat-trick of major domestic individual awards.<ref name=":21" />

A total of 13 current City players were selected for squads for [[UEFA Euro 2024|Euro 2024]], the joint-most alongside [[Inter Milan]], and one player was selected for the [[2024 Copa América]]. Both competitions would be played during June and July 2024.<ref>{{cite news |date=8 June 2024 |title=City players in Euro 2024 and Copa America squads |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/euro-2024-copa-america-squads-63852497 |access-date=8 June 2024 |publisher=Manchester City F.C.}}</ref>

==Pre-season and friendlies==
On 20 April 2023, Manchester City announced a tour of [[South Korea]] as part of the pre-season preparations in July, where they would take on [[Atlético Madrid]] in the ''[[Coupang]] Play Series''. This tour was the first time City visited South Korea since 1976.<ref>{{cite news|last=Pollard|first=Rob|title=City set for South Korea as part of 2023/24 preseason tour|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/manchester-city-atletico-madrid-south-korea-63817566|date=20 April 2023|access-date=20 April 2023|publisher=Manchester City F.C.}}</ref> The club later announced that two friendlies against [[Yokohama F. Marinos]], a fellow [[City Football Group|CFG]] club, and [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]], who City [[2022–23 Manchester City F.C. season#Pre-season and friendlies|faced a year ago]] in the [[United States]], would take place in [[Tokyo]] before the team traveled to South Korea.<ref>{{cite news|last=Johnson|first=Isaac|title=Man City announce two more friendlies for pre-season Asia tour including Bayern Munich fixture|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/manchester-city-preseason-yokohama-bayern-26924295|date=16 May 2023|access-date=16 May 2023|publisher=Manchester Evening News}}</ref>

====Matches====
The league fixtures were released on 15 June 2023.<ref>{{cite news |title=Premier League 2023/24 fixtures released |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/3537201 |date=15 June 2023 |access-date=15 June 2023 |publisher=Premier League}}</ref>{{efn|Note: The Premier League website includes a number of incorrect attendance figures, which may have been based upon best-guesses, as City rarely released attendance figures to the public following (and including) the Burnley home game early in 2024. The attendance figures included in the statistics below are taken from the official Manchester City match programme from the game against West Ham United on 19 May 2024. The crowd figure against West Ham has been estimated based upon stadium capacity and has yet to be verified by Manchester City.

For further evidence of the above, reported attendances of 55,097 for the Manchester United and West Ham home games significantly exceed the stadium's current working capacity and have seemingly been estimated by unknown sources using an outdated capacity that includes a number of since removed seats and others that were unsold due to segregation issues.}}

===FA Cup===
{{main|2023–24 FA Cup}}
[[File:FA Cup Final.jpg|thumb|right|[[Wembley Stadium]] during the FA Cup final]]

As a Premier League team, Manchester City entered the FA Cup in the third round proper, and were drawn at home to [[EFL Championship]] side [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]].<ref>{{cite news|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67606817|title=FA Cup third-round draw: Arsenal v Liverpool, Sunderland v Newcastle, Wigan v Man Utd, Man City v Huddersfield|date=3 December 2023|work=BBC Sport|access-date=4 December 2023}}</ref> In the fourth round, City were drawn away to fellow Premier League side [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]].<ref>{{cite news |title=City learn FA Cup Fourth Round opponents |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/manchester-city-fa-cup-fourth-round-opponents-63840331 |access-date=8 January 2024 |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |date=8 January 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=City's FA Cup tie at Spurs to be televised live |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/tottenham-v-manchester-city-fa-cup-4th-round-tie-date-announced-63840583 |date=11 January 2024 |access-date=11 January 2024 |publisher=Manchester City F.C.}}</ref> In the fifth round, they were again drawn away to a fellow Premier League side in [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Maidstone drawn at Sheff Wed or Coventry in FA Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/68122439 |date=28 January 2024 |access-date=28 January 2024 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Date and TV details for FA Cup tie with Luton confirmed |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/fa-cup-fifth-round-luton-v-city-date-confirmed-63842230 |access-date=7 February 2024 |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |date=2 February 2024}}</ref> In the quarter-finals, the Blues were drawn at home to fellow Premier League side [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]]. In the semi-finals at [[Wembley Stadium]], City were paired with [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], with a potential [[Manchester derby]] and rematch of [[2023 FA Cup final|last year's final]] at stake, which eventually proved to be the case.

===FIFA Club World Cup===
{{main|2023 FIFA Club World Cup}}
Manchester City entered the tournament in the semi-finals as the European representative, having been drawn against the winner of the quarter-final match between [[Club León]] and [[Urawa Red Diamonds]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Man City learn Club World Cup draw fate |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/teams/manchester-city |access-date=5 September 2023 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=5 September 2023}}</ref>
